sections.content: How many people stayed in Halifax after gaining qualifications?

Halifax is a large town in Yorkshire and The Humber. Halifax does not have its own university.

Halifax has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Halifax ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 4,655 state-school pupils from Halifax who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 1,330 (29%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 1,485 (32%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Halifax to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Halifax's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Halifax in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Halifax move to?

Of Halifax's graduates, 380 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 75 of those graduates (20%) were living fairly locally, in the Halifax travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Halifax's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 325 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 110 of those qualified non-graduates (34%) were living fairly locally, in the Halifax travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Halifax's GCSE cohort:

  • 195 graduates left Yorkshire and The Humber
  • the most common region they moved to was the North West
  • 95 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left Yorkshire and The Humber
  • the most common region they moved to was the North West

In 2018 to 2019, 22% of graduates and 21% of qualified non-graduates living in Halifax had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 1,195 graduates and 1,430 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Halifax. This is compared with the 1,330 graduates and 1,485 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 78% of the graduates had also lived in Halifax as GCSE pupils, while 22% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Halifax in 2018 to 2019, 79% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 21% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
